title: Surgical carveout: console compact trace + cost MVP cuts and acceptance criteria
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Context: We need a tightly scoped MVP for Console insights (dashboards, tracing quickpath, and cost breakdown) that meets an internal GA gating metric: provide near-term visibility for SLO regressions and top-line route cost deltas while keeping storage and compute costs within current budget targets. This ticket captures the 'surgical carveout' decisions made to reduce scope, the acceptance criteria for the trimmed surface, and the rollout constraints.

Scope trimmed for MVP (explicit cuts):
- Dashboards: ship 3 aggregated tiles only (Route Health, Token Cost per Route, Error Rate by Region). Remove per-tenant cohorting, per-model breakdowns, and user-segment filters for MVP.
- Tracing: implement shallow trace capture (sampling at 1% by default) with a lightweight span schema that excludes raw prompt/response payloads. No trace flamegraph or deep interactive span explorer in MVP. Provide a redirect to existing tracing system for heavy investigations.
- Cost breakdown: provide aggregated cost buckets at the route level and a 7-day retention window. No per-token-by-model history or hourly resolution for MVP.
- Storage/retention: limit telemetry retention to 7 days and disable long-term storage pipelines for the MVP cohort to control cost.
- Rollouts & fallback: include a read-only degraded ‘compact mode’ when telemetry ingestion exceeds budgeted thresholds. No canary multi-tenant rollouts for MVP (single-tenant internal testing first).

Included in MVP (kept surface):
- Per-route aggregated metrics and simple trend sparklines (7-day).
- Minimal trace link: a single trace id that links to the tracing service for sampled traces.
- Cost tile: aggregated route-level cost and tokens-per-route over 7 days.
- Alerting hooks: support one alert rule template (Route latency spike).

Non-functional objectives:
- Dashboard load time target: < 600ms for the 3 tiles on a 95th percentile basis for typical orgs (<= 10K requests/day).
- Extra storage/compute budget: must not exceed 15% above current observability spend for the pilot cohort.

Out-of-scope (explicit): per-user dashboards, cross-org comparisons, model-attribution cost, function calling trace details, full stack flamegraphs, export to S3, and long-term retention analytics.
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Decision made during triage: prioritize high-leverage tiles that answer the most common operator questions (did latency increase, which route drove cost, are there regional errors). 2026-03-12: PM/Eng/Design alignment confirmed the sampling-first tracing approach to avoid prompt leakage and control storage. 2026-03-12: Design accepted compact visual language (single metric tiles + sparklines) to keep implementation shallow. Links: https://docs.internal/redwood/console-mvp-snapshot (PRD), https://drive.redwood.com/d/console-mvp-designs (design mocks).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Three dashboard tiles (Route Health, Token Cost per Route, Error Rate by Region) exist and populate with live data for a test org. 2) Tiles load under 600ms p95 on staging with synthetic traffic that mimics 10K req/day. 3) Tracing sampling is configurable and defaults to 1%; sampled traces produce a trace id link visible in the route inspector. 4) No prompt/response payloads are stored in traces or logs for MVP. 5) Cost tile shows aggregated cost for each route for the last 7 days and matches billing reconciliation within a 5% delta during smoke tests. 6) Retention policy enforces 7-day TTL for all telemetry ingested by the MVP pipeline. 7) Compact fallback mode triggers and serves read-only dashboards when ingestion budget breaches threshold and is documented in runbook. 8) Design sign-off obtained from Design lead and PM acceptance verified in staging. 9) Security review checklist completed (data handling & PII) and marked in the ticket (security_review_required=false recorded because no PII stored).
notes: Implementation trade-offs: engineering recommended removing per-model attribution to avoid complex joins across billing and traces; we accepted this to meet target ship date. If we observe higher customer demand for model-level cost, follow-up ticket will be created to reintroduce model attribution in a filtered, on-demand view. Monitoring: add a metering dashboard to track telemetry ingestion rate vs budget and surface this as an internal alert before the compact fallback is activated. Post-MVP: plan a 6-week evaluation window to validate the 7-day retention and cost assumptions and decide whether to extend retention or add rollup pipelines.
